summary: spec : Warn when --spec-draft-p-min is used with probabilistic draft sampling ( #31294 ) spec : skip p_min for sampled MTP and DFlash2 drafts Under rejection sampling the acceptance at a position is 1 - TV(p, q), which the draft's top probability does not tell, so the p_min cutoff dropped draft tokens the target would have accepted. Skip it when MTP or DFlash2 samples the draft. draft-simple keeps it: each extra draft token costs a full draft model pass. spec : replace the sampled-draft p_min skip with a warning p_min behaves as on master again for every drafter and sampling mode. Instead, log a warning when --spec-draft-p-min > 0 is used with --spec-draft-sampling probabilistic, suggesting p_min 0: under rejection sampling the draft's top probability does not tell how much of the draft the target accepts. The cut is not skipped because with MTP at long drafts it can still pay off. spec : warn about p_min only for drafters that use it The n-gram drafters ignore p_min, and DSpark uses it as the cutoff of its confidence head, so the warning is skipped when only these are configured. summary: Release v5.21.0 New Model additions MiniCPM-OCR MiniCPM-OCR is a document-understanding model from OpenBMB's MiniCPM-V family. It keeps the MiniCPM-V 4.6 architecture, which pairs a SigLIP vision encoder and a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model. It is specialized for reading text-dense images such as scanned pages, screenshots, receipts and tables. Links: Documentation | Paper Feat test ( #49920 ) by @guarin in #49920 Flint Flint is Recursive's mixture-of-experts language model. Compared to a standard SwiGLU MoE transformer such as Qwen3-MoE, it uses hybrid attention (sliding-window attention with rotary embeddings over the current token and the previous 512 tokens in most layers, and full attention without positional encoding in the remaining layers). It also has learned attention sinks, as in GPT-OSS, with per-head RMS-normalized queries and keys. Each sparse layer routes a token to 6 of 256 experts by sigmoid score and adds an ungated shared expert, and the first two layers are dense. Links: Documentation Add Flint model support. summary: ONNX Runtime 1.30.0 expands generative AI inference, improves CPU and GPU performance, adds Go bindings, and strengthens runtime reliability. These notes cover changes since ONNX Runtime 1.29.1. Highlights Expanded CUDA inference support with variable-length causal convolution for continuous batching, speculative decoding in paged XQA, and INT4 paged KV caches with per-channel scales ( #32168 , #32340 , #32515 ). Improved WebGPU PagedAttention, added GPT-OSS support and INT8 KV-cache block quantization, and extended convolution optimizations ( #31727 , #32277 , #32284 , #32420 ). Added fused CPU LinearAttention kernels for AVX-512, Arm64 NEON, and SVE, plus AVX2 LayerNorm/RMSNorm acceleration ( #31674 , #31973 , #32178 , #32356 ). Added Go bindings for the ONNX Runtime C API and DeepSeek Engram contrib operators ( #29615 , #32268 ). Source builds can opt out with -Donnxruntime_USE_FP4_QMOE=OFF ( #32096 , #32163 ).
